name: Mightier
one_liner: Video games played with a heart-rate sensor that get harder as a child gets upset, so kids practise calming down; monthly subscription.
best_for: Parents of children who struggle with anger, frustration or meltdowns
Children with ADHD or autism who need practice calming down, alongside other care
Families who can use HSA or FSA funds for a home program
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
Children who need assessment or treatment from a clinician for severe behavior problems
Families who want to avoid third-party advertising cookies and tracking
short_description: Biofeedback video games for kids: a heart sensor makes the game harder when the child's heart rate rises, teaching calming skills. $28–$40 a month.
long_description: Mightier is a home program of video games played while wearing a heart-rate sensor. When a child's heart rate rises the game gets harder, so they practise calming strategies to keep playing. A kit includes the sensor, conversation cards and access to 25+ games; you can use a compatible device or add Mightier's own game-only device for $75, and parents get an app to track progress and manage screen time. Plans cost $40 a month, $34 a month billed for 6 months, or $28 a month billed yearly, with a 90-day money-back guarantee, and can be paid with HSA or FSA funds. Mightier grew out of Boston Children's Hospital research on a game called RAGE-Control; a 2021 pilot randomized trial of RAGE-Control in 40 youth found clinician- and parent-rated improvements but no difference in children's self-rated anger. We did not find a peer-reviewed study of the Mightier product itself. Its privacy policy allows third-party advertising cookies, and deletion rights are limited to some jurisdictions and to parents of children under 13.
patient_summary: Your child plays video games while wearing a heart-rate sensor; when they get worked up the game gets harder, so they practise calming down to keep playing. You track progress in the parent app. Plans run $28–$40 a month depending on billing period, with a 90-day money-back guarantee and HSA/FSA payment accepted.

pricing.notes: 6-month plan $34/month ($204). Optional game-only device +$75. 90-day money-back guarantee (shipping not refunded). HSA/FSA and some state education savings accounts accepted.

privacy.notes: Policy allows third-party advertisers to place cookies for targeted ads and the parent app reports usage data used to track; deletion only in some jurisdictions or for children under 13.

faqs.a: Mightier is a biofeedback-based video game platform for children ages 6-14 that teaches emotional regulation using a heart rate sensor and 30+ interactive games developed from research at Boston Children's Hospital.

Children wear a Bluetooth heart rate sensor while playing games. When their heart rate increases from stress or frustration, games become harder, encouraging them to practice calming techniques to regain control and continue playing.

faqs.q: What results can families expect from Mightier?
faqs.a: After 3 months, 84% of parents report improvements in anger, frustration, or aggressive behaviors, and 71% report improvements in impulsivity and/or hyperactivity.
Mightier costs $28-$40 per month with a 90-day money-back guarantee. It is HSA/FSA eligible.

primary_uses: Anger and meltdown management for kids
Emotional regulation practice for children with ADHD or autism
Parent tracking of progress and screen time
